components.name: 1. index.html app shell + anti-flash theme boot
components.purpose: Single static shell that both the SPA (#app) and the server-rendered SEO pages (#app-embed, injected by seo-content.js via server.js's pageShell()) load. Must apply the correct theme before first paint and must NOT hardcode the Google Maps script tag, because the browser key only becomes known after GET /api/config resolves.

components.name: 2. Theme token system (5 themes + follow-system) and matching Google Maps styles[]
components.purpose: One CSS custom-property contract every component consumes, plus a JS table pairing each theme with a Maps JS `styles[]` array so the map canvas itself recolors, not just the chrome around it.

components.name: 3. Full-screen map layout: canvas, category chips, results list, pin/card sync, responsive behavior
components.purpose: The core screen. Map, chips and results must feel like one instrument: selecting in either the list or the map drives the other, and the whole thing has to work as a phone-first layout since this is a GPS app.

components.name: 4. Business detail panel (photos, rating, hours, phone, directions, reviews with Google attribution)
components.purpose: Render GET /api/place?id= into the results-panel's detail view (desktop) / expanded bottom sheet (mobile), with legally-compliant Google review attribution.

components.name: 5. Geolocation flow (permission, denied/timeout/insecure, manual fallback via /api/geocode)
components.purpose: Get a lat/lng to drive /api/nearby, with an honest, specific message for every failure mode and a working manual-entry escape hatch.

components.name: 6. Filter UI: open now, minimum rating, radius, sort
components.purpose: Give users control over the up-to-20 results GET /api/nearby returns, matching exactly what the current field masks make available.

components.name: 7. Auth views, friends view (friends-only, mutual-accept), saved-places view
components.purpose: Match the exact request/response shapes server.js exposes for /api/auth/*, /api/friends/*, /api/saved.

components.name: 8. Header / hero (owner's Option D copy)
components.purpose: First-touch marketing block for logged-out / first-time visitors on the app itself, without getting in the way of the core map on repeat visits.
components.design:
```html

Find great places. Bring people with you.

Search every kind of business near you, save the ones worth returning to, and see where your friends are headed.

Get started — it's free Browse without an account
``` ```js function shouldShowHero() { if (state.user) return false; return !sessionStorage.getItem('bf-hero-seen'); } function dismissHero() { sessionStorage.setItem('bf-hero-seen', '1'); heroEl.remove(); } ``` Shown above the category row on `#/map` only when logged out and not yet dismissed this session; auto-dismisses (calls `dismissHero()`) the moment the user picks a category or a search resolves, so it never covers the map on the second interaction. `.hero-accent` is styled with `color: var(--accent)`, keeping the same Option D copy legible and on-brand across all 5 themes without hardcoding a color. This markup is intentionally the same fragment the SEO team can reuse verbatim above `#app-embed` if they want the same headline on landing pages — kept as a small exported `renderHero()` in `public/js/views/hero.js` rather than inlined in one view file.

components.name: 9. State management, hash router, module layout, XSS-safe rendering discipline
components.purpose: A framework-free but disciplined SPA: one state object, a small router, one escaping rule that's actually followed everywhere, matching the zero-dependency constraint.

risks: Photo rendering gap: server.js's /api/place returns place.photos as an array of Places API *resource names* (e.g. 'places/XXXX/photos/YYYY'), not URLs. There is no /api/photo proxy route in server.js, and the browser-facing GOOGLE_MAPS_BROWSER_KEY is documented (.env.example) as referrer-restricted with no Places scope, so the frontend cannot legally or technically turn those names into images by itself. This design wires the gallery to call a not-yet-existing '/api/photo?name=...&w=...' endpoint and degrades to a placeholder icon on failure, but a backend specialist must add a server-side proxy through SERVER_KEY (https://places.googleapis.com/v1/{photoName}/media?maxWidthPx=...) — with its own cost cap — or photos will never render.

'Open now' filter cannot work as a list filter today: GET /api/nearby's Places field mask (in placesNearby()) does not include regularOpeningHours/openNow — only GET /api/place (details) does. The filter UI is designed to activate automatically the moment that field is added to the Nearby field mask, but flagging this now because adding it is a *billing-tier* change (opening-hours data is priced as Pro/Enterprise+Atmosphere data in Places API New), so it needs an explicit decision from whoever owns the cost caps, not a silent frontend fix.

Google review attribution requires Google's own provided logo asset (not a custom recreation) per the Places API attribution policy. This design references /assets/google-on-white.png as a placeholder path; before shipping, someone must download Google's actual attribution mark from Google's Places API branding guidelines and place it under public/assets/, and pick the on-white vs on-non-white variant per theme (some themes here — midnight, mono — are dark/near-black surfaces where the on-white lockup would need the on-non-white variant instead).

server.js currently requires('./seo-content') for { seoPages, categoryList }, and that file does not exist yet, so the server cannot boot at all right now. This frontend design was produced by static reading of server.js/store.js only — it has not been run against a live server and cannot be, until seo-content.js exists. The public/app.js dual-mount design (full #app vs seo #app-embed) depends on seo-content.js's pageShell() continuing to render `<div id="app-embed" data-category="...">` exactly as it does today; if the SEO specialist changes that container's id/attributes, embed.js's mount detection breaks silently.

Radius filter changes must re-call GET /api/nearby (server enforces the circle radius, capped at 50000m and consuming the shared NEARBY_DAILY_CAP) rather than being a pure client-side filter; combined with category switches and geolocation retries, an aggressive user could burn through the daily nearby cap quickly. The design debounces radius/category changes (~400ms) but does not itself add caching — worth confirming with whoever owns store.js's tryConsume caps whether client-side result caching per (lat,lng,category,radius) bucket is also expected to reduce calls.

priceLevel from Places API (New) is a string enum (e.g. 'PRICE_LEVEL_MODERATE'), not the old numeric 1-4 — the design includes a PRICE_LABEL mapping table, but this must stay in sync if the backend ever changes the field mask or Google renames enum values.

Zero build step + CDN-loaded Google Maps JS means the map's availability depends entirely on GOOGLE_MAPS_BROWSER_KEY being present and referrer-restricted correctly in Cloud Console; this design handles the !live (no key) case by skipping the Maps JS load and showing a placeholder, but it cannot detect a *misconfigured* (wrong-referrer) key client-side — that will surface as a silent grey map with a console error from Google's script, which is worth a follow-up UX affordance (e.g. an onerror handler on the dynamically injected <script> tag) if that failure mode matters to the owner.
summary: Read server.js and data/store.js in full to ground the design in the real API contract, then specified the complete public/ frontend as 9 components with concrete code: an index.html shell with an inline anti-flash theme script that also has to dual-boot into either the full SPA (#app) or the lightweight SEO-page embed widget (#app-embed) that seo-content.js's server-rendered pages inject; a 5-theme + follow-system CSS custom-property token system with full hex palettes (aurora, midnight, meadow, sunset, mono) each paired with a matching Google Maps styles[] JSON array so the map canvas itself recolors; a mobile-first full-screen map layout (desktop sidebar / mobile draggable bottom sheet, horizontally-scrolling category chips) with a single selectPlace() function driving both pin-click-highlights-card and card-click-pans-map; a business detail panel with photos, hours, phone/directions/website, and a Google-reviews list built with the required author name/photo/profile-link/Google-logo attribution, using DOM-construction (never innerHTML+string concat) for anything sourced from Google or other users; a geolocation flow with exact copy for idle/requesting/granted/denied/timeout/unsupported/insecure states plus a manual /api/geocode fallback; a filter bar (open now, min rating, radius, sort) that correctly distinguishes which filters can run client-side over the already-fetched 20 results versus which require a re-fetch; auth/friends/saved views matching server.js's exact request/response shapes, including the friends-only 'no stranger discovery' framing in the UI copy; the owner's locked Option D hero copy, shown only to logged-out first-time visitors; and a state/router/module architecture (plain pub-sub state object, regex hash router, one api.js per endpoint, one el()/esc() discipline) — all vanilla ES modules, zero npm dependencies, no build step, matching the project's locked stack. Surfaced several concrete cross-cutting gaps between the existing server API and what this design needs (no photo-proxy endpoint for the Places photo resource names, 'open now' missing from the Nearby field mask, missing Google attribution asset, and the fact server.js currently can't boot because seo-content.js doesn't exist yet) as risks for the other specialists rather than silently working around them.
